title: Tokenization
subtitle: How text becomes tokens, BPE, and counting tokens

content.text: LLMs do not operate on characters or words. They use subword tokenization (BPE or similar) which breaks text into variable-length chunks.

content.code:
import tiktoken  # OpenAI tokenizer

enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("gpt-4")
tokens = enc.encode("Hello, world!")
print(tokens)      # [9906, 11, 1917, 0]
print(len(tokens)) # 4

# Anthropic token count via API
import anthropic
client = anthropic.Anthropic()
count = client.messages.count_tokens(
    model="claude-opus-4-5",
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Hello, world!"}]
)
print(count.input_tokens)

content.text: Code uses more tokens per character than English. A Python function of 100 characters may use 50-80 tokens.

questions.question: Why does tokenization matter for LLM costs?
options: LLMs charge per second of compute
API pricing is based on input and output token count
More tokens make models less accurate
questions.explanation: LLM API pricing is based on tokens in and out. Understanding tokenization helps estimate and control costs.

faq.a: Yes. Claude, GPT-4, and Llama use different tokenizers. Never assume token counts transfer between providers.
